paragraphs: AdaptHealth Corp. and subsidiaries ("AdaptHealth" or "the Company") is a national leader in providing patient-centered, healthcare-at-home solutions including home medical equipment ("HME"), medical supplies, and related services. The Company operates under four reportable segments that align with its product categories: (i) Sleep Health, (ii) Respiratory Health, (iii) Diabetes Health, and (iv) Wellness at Home. A description of the products and services provided within each of the Company's four reportable segments is provided below.

The Sleep Health segment provides sleep therapy equipment, supplies and related services (including continuous positive airway pressure and BiLevel services) to individuals for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea.

The Respiratory Health segment provides oxygen and home mechanical ventilation equipment and supplies and related chronic therapy services to individuals for the treatment of respiratory diseases, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and chronic respiratory failure.
The Diabetes Health segment provides medical devices, including continuous glucose monitors and insulin pumps, and related services to patients for the treatment of diabetes.

The Wellness at Home segment provides home medical equipment and services to patients in their homes including those who have been discharged from acute care and other facilities. The segment tailors a service model to patients who are adjusting to new lifestyles or navigating complex disease states by providing essential medical supplies and durable medical equipment.

The Company services beneficiaries of Medicare, Medicaid and commercial insurance payors. As of December 31, 2025, AdaptHealth serviced approximately 4.3 million patients annually in all 50 states through our network of approximately 640 locations in 48 states. The Company's principal executive offices are located at 555 East North Lane, Suite 5075, Conshohocken, Pennsylvania 19428.

Product Offering. AdaptHealth delivers patient-centered, healthcare-at-home solutions including home medical equipment, medical supplies, and related services directly to a patient's home upon discharge from a hospital and/or receipt of a physician/medical referral. The breadth of AdaptHealth's products is particularly valuable to acute care hospitals, sleep laboratories and long-term care facilities that discharge patients with complex conditions and multiple product needs.

For resupply sale and one-time sale products, which include those deemed to be consumables, AdaptHealth receives a single payment upon sale of the product. These products, which include positive airway pressure ("PAP") masks and related supplies, continuous glucose monitors ("CGM"), diabetes management supplies, orthopedic bracing, wound care supplies, home medical equipment and related accessories, incontinence supplies, medications, enteral supplies, and other products, accounted for approximately 63% of AdaptHealth's net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.

AdaptHealth is paid a fixed monthly amount for certain HME products as designated by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services ("CMS") or commercial insurance payors, such as oxygen and home mechanical ventilation equipment, PAP equipment, hospital beds, and other products. These sales accounted for approximately 33% of AdaptHealth's net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.

AdaptHealth receives a per member per month ("PMPM") fee under certain at-risk capitation arrangements, which refers to a model in which the Company receives a PMPM fee from the third-party payor, and is responsible for

managing a range of healthcare services and associated costs of its members. In at-risk capitation arrangements, AdaptHealth is responsible for the cost of contracted healthcare services required by those members in accordance with the terms of each agreement. Capitated revenue contracts with payors are generally multi-year arrangements and have a single monthly stand ready performance obligation to provide all aspects of necessary medical care to members for the contracted period in accordance with the scope of the agreements. These at-risk capitation arrangements accounted for approximately 4.0% of AdaptHealth's net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.

Supply Chain. AdaptHealth plays an important role in delivering HME products to patients in their homes. Manufacturers of home medical equipment and diabetes medical devices sell and ship their products to AdaptHealth directly. AdaptHealth also contracts with national healthcare distribution companies to ship certain HME products and diabetes medical devices directly to patients' homes. These distributors invoice AdaptHealth for the cost of shipped products at the time of sale. AdaptHealth receives referrals from a variety of sources, such as acute care hospitals, sleep laboratories, pulmonologist and endocrinologist offices, skilled nursing facilities, hospice operators, and primary care providers, among others. AdaptHealth's products are either shipped to patients' homes by AdaptHealth-operated or contracted delivery trucks or shipped using proprietary or third-party distribution services. AdaptHealth invoices payors and patients directly for the products that are delivered and for the services that are provided.

Management. AdaptHealth is led by a proven management team with experience across a variety of organizations in the healthcare industry. AdaptHealth's management structure is strategically aligned through its four reportable segments, which each have a general manager who are responsible for the operations of each segment. These general managers report to AdaptHealth's Chief Operating Officer. AdaptHealth has a centralized approach for key business processes, including revenue cycle management, purchasing, payor contracting, mergers and acquisitions ("M&A") activity, finance, compliance, legal, human resources, IT, resupply and sales management. However, AdaptHealth believes that the personalized nature of patient care and referral relationships, characteristic of the home healthcare industry, also requires a focus on operating locally as well. AdaptHealth responds promptly and effectively to local market demands and opportunities through local managers, who are responsible and accountable for maintaining and developing relationships with referral sources and serving patients.

IT. AdaptHealth has established an integrated, technology-enabled, centralized platform, distinguishing itself from many of its competitors that traditionally use less automated processes that are typically complex, can be prone to mistakes and are less efficient. AdaptHealth's technology enables automated, compliant, and integrated workflow into patients' delivery of care. AdaptHealth believes that this advanced technology platform provides it with a competitive advantage through its unique components that cater to patients and physicians. AdaptHealth believes that its technology platform has several characteristics that appeal to physicians, including its ease of use, the improved compliance it enables through its integrated systems, and the automated, integrated workflow it provides for patients' delivery of care. AdaptHealth has formed close relationships with its third-party software providers to optimize its workflow. Additionally, AdaptHealth's e-prescribing capabilities enhance transparency and reduce transcription and other errors. AdaptHealth believes that patients are also better served due to the efficiency from time of order to delivery and the seamless integration across points of care enabled by AdaptHealth's platform. The integrated system also provides AdaptHealth management with critical information in a timely manner, allowing them to track performance levels company wide. AdaptHealth utilizes a proprietary mobile delivery technology called OTL, which has many features, including delivery notification, patient satisfaction applications and referral source notifications.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
Reliance on relatively few suppliers for the majority of AdaptHealth's patient service equipment and supplies could adversely affect its ability to operate.
Supply chain disruptions and economy-wide labor shortages in the U.S. have negatively impacted, and may continue to negatively impact, AdaptHealth's businesses.
AdaptHealth has been, and may continue to be, negatively impacted by inflation and rising interest rates.
AdaptHealth's results of operations may be adversely impacted if expenses under capitated agreements exceed revenues.
AdaptHealth's payor contracts are subject to renegotiation or termination, which could result in a decrease in AdaptHealth's revenue or profits.
Changes made by payors to the way they cover products supplied by AdaptHealth could have an adverse impact on AdaptHealth's revenue and operations.
Changes in governmental or private payor supply replenishment schedules could adversely affect AdaptHealth.
If AdaptHealth fails to manage the complex and lengthy reimbursement process, its revenue, financial condition and results of operations could suffer.
AdaptHealth may be adversely affected by consolidation among health insurers and other industry participants.
If AdaptHealth is unable to maintain or develop relationships with patient referral sources, its growth and profitability could be adversely affected.
Changes in medical equipment technology and development of new treatments may cause AdaptHealth's current equipment or services to become obsolete.
AdaptHealth's strategic growth plan, which historically involved the acquisition of other companies, may not succeed.
AdaptHealth's revenue could be impacted by federal and state changes to reimbursement and other Medicaid and Medicare policies.
paragraphs: We operate in a rapidly changing environment that involves a number of risks. The following discussion highlights some of these risks and others are discussed elsewhere in this report. These and other risks could materially adversely affect our business, revenue, financial condition and results of operations. Additional risk factors not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business or results of operations.

AdaptHealth currently relies on a relatively small number of suppliers to provide it with the majority of its patient service equipment and supplies. Significant price increases, or disruptions in the ability to obtain such equipment and supplies from existing suppliers, may force AdaptHealth to use alternative suppliers. Additionally, trade policy developments, including ongoing investigations, could result in new tariffs on imported medical equipment or components, which could increase the costs of manufacturing or procuring patient service equipment and supplies. Such tariffs or any new excise taxes imposed on manufacturers of certain medical equipment could be passed on to customers, such as AdaptHealth. Such manufacturers may be forced to make other changes to their products or manufacturing processes that are unacceptable to AdaptHealth, resulting in a need to change suppliers. Any change in suppliers AdaptHealth uses could cause delays in the delivery of such products and possible losses in revenue, which could adversely affect AdaptHealth's results of operations. In addition, alternative suppliers may not be available, or may not provide their products and services at similar or favorable prices. If AdaptHealth cannot obtain the patient service equipment and supplies it currently uses, or alternatives at similar or favorable prices, AdaptHealth's ability to provide such products may be severely impacted, which could have an adverse effect on its business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flow, capital resources and liquidity.

Many companies, including AdaptHealth, have experienced supply chain and labor challenges. Materials, equipment and labor shortages, shipping, logistics and other delays and other supply chain and related disruptions may make it more difficult and costly for AdaptHealth to obtain products or services from third parties. If these types of disruptions occur, a material adverse effect on AdaptHealth's business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows could result. Continued labor shortages have driven a significant increase in competition throughout the industry to attract and retain talent and have also led to increased labor costs.

Union activity is another factor that may contribute to increased labor costs. AdaptHealth currently has a minimal number of union employees, so an increase in labor union activity could have a significant impact on AdaptHealth's labor costs. AdaptHealth's failure to recruit and retain qualified employees, or to control its labor costs, could have a material adverse effect on its business, financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.

While AdaptHealth seeks to mitigate any cost increases, labor impacts and supply chain delays and shortages, these efforts may not be successful and AdaptHealth may experience adverse impacts due to such factors. AdaptHealth cannot predict the extent of these current trends or other future increases in operating costs. To the extent such costs continue to increase, AdaptHealth may be prevented, in whole or in part, from passing such cost increases through to its existing and prospective customers, or AdaptHealth's customers may seek other competitive sources due to supply chain delays, which could have a material adverse impact on AdaptHealth's business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

Increases in inflation have had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on AdaptHealth. Current and future inflationary effects may be driven by, among other things, general inflationary cost increases, supply chain disruptions and governmental stimulus or fiscal policies. The cost to manufacture and distribute the equipment and products that AdaptHealth purchases from vendors and provides to patients may be influenced by inflationary pressures and the cost of materials, labor, shipping, and transportation, including fuel costs. The cost of equipment and products may also be impacted by a shortage in the availability of certain products. Additionally, it is not certain that AdaptHealth will be able to pass increased costs onto customers to offset inflationary pressures. Increases in inflation could have an impact on the overall demand for AdaptHealth's products and services, its costs for labor, equipment and products, and the margins it is able to realize on its products, all of which could have an adverse impact on AdaptHealth's business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows. In addition, future volatility of general price inflation and the impact of inflation on costs and availability of materials, costs for shipping and warehousing, workforce wage pressure, and other operational overhead could adversely affect AdaptHealth's financial results. Although there have been recent increases in inflation, AdaptHealth cannot predict whether these trends will continue. AdaptHealth's primary mitigation efforts relating to these inflationary pressures include utilizing AdaptHealth's purchasing power in negotiations with vendors and the increased use of technology to drive operating efficiencies and control costs, such as AdaptHealth's digital platform for prescriptions, orders and delivery.

The Respiratory Health segment provides oxygen and home mechanical ventilation equipment and supplies and related chronic therapy services to individuals for the treatment of respiratory diseases, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and chronic respiratory failure.
The Diabetes Health segment provides medical devices, including continuous glucose monitors and insulin pumps, and related services to patients for the treatment of diabetes.

The Wellness at Home segment provides home medical equipment and services to patients in their homes including those who have been discharged from acute care and other facilities. The segment tailors a service model to patients who are adjusting to new lifestyles or navigating complex disease states by providing essential medical supplies and durable medical equipment.

The Company services beneficiaries of Medicare, Medicaid and commercial insurance payors. The cost to manufacture and distribute the equipment and products that AdaptHealth purchases from vendors and provides to patients is influenced by the cost of materials, labor, shipping, and transportation, including fuel costs. Current and future inflationary effects may be driven by, among other things, general inflationary cost increases, supply chain disruptions and governmental stimulus or fiscal policies. Increases in inflation could impact the overall demand for AdaptHealth's products and services, availability of materials, its costs for labor, equipment and products, shipping, warehousing and other operational overhead and the margins it is able to realize on its products, all of which could have an adverse impact on AdaptHealth's business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows. Additionally, it is not certain whether AdaptHealth would be able to pass increased costs onto customers to offset inflationary pressures. AdaptHealth has experienced inflationary pressure and higher costs as a result of increased cost of materials, labor, shipping and transportation. Although there have been increases in inflation, AdaptHealth cannot predict whether these trends will continue. AdaptHealth's mitigation efforts relating to these inflationary pressures include utilizing AdaptHealth's purchasing power in negotiations with vendors and the increased use of technology to drive operating efficiencies and control costs, such as AdaptHealth's digital platform for prescriptions, orders and delivery.

Net Revenue. Net revenue is recognized for services and related products that AdaptHealth provides to patients for healthcare-at-home solutions including HME, medical supplies and related services. Revenues are recognized either at a point in time for the sale of supplies and consumables, over the service period for equipment rental (including, but not limited to, PAP machines, hospital beds, wheelchairs and other equipment), net of implicit price concessions for amounts estimated to be received from patients or under reimbursement arrangements with Medicare, Medicaid and other third-party payors, including private insurers, or in the month in which eligible members are entitled to receive healthcare services in connection with at-risk capitation arrangements. Certain trends or uncertainties that may have a material impact on revenue growth and operating results include the Company's ability to obtain new at-risk capitation arrangements, new patient starts and to generate referrals from patient referral sources and the ability to meet the increased demand considering inflationary pressures.

Cost of Net Revenue. Cost of net revenue primarily includes the cost of non-capitalized medical equipment and supplies, distribution expenses, labor costs, facilities and vehicle rental costs, and depreciation for capitalized patient equipment. Distribution expenses represent the cost incurred to coordinate and deliver products and services to the patients. Included in distribution expenses are leasing, maintenance, licensing and fuel costs for the vehicle fleet; salaries, benefits and other costs related to drivers and dispatch personnel; and amounts paid to couriers.

General and Administrative Expenses. General and administrative expenses consist of corporate support costs including revenue cycle management costs, information technology, human resources, finance, contracting, legal, compliance, equity-based compensation, and other administrative costs.

Depreciation and Amortization, Excluding Patient Equipment Depreciation. Depreciation expense includes depreciation charges for capital assets other than patient equipment (which is included as part of the cost of net revenue). Amortization expense includes amortization of identifiable intangible assets.
AdaptHealth's operating results and financial performance are influenced by certain unique events during the periods discussed herein, including the following:

AdaptHealth has a significant amount of goodwill on its balance sheet that resulted from the business acquisitions AdaptHealth has made. Goodwill is not amortized, rather, it is assessed at the reporting unit level for impairment annually and also upon the occurrence of a triggering event or change in circumstances indicating that the carrying value of goodwill may be impaired. A significant amount of judgment is involved in determining if an indicator of impairment has occurred. Such triggering events potentially warranting an annual or interim goodwill impairment assessment include, among other factors, declines in historical or projected reporting unit revenue, operating results or cash flows, and sustained decreases in AdaptHealth's stock price or market capitalization. Such changes in circumstance can include, among others, changes in the legal environment, reimbursement environment, operating performance, and/or future prospects. AdaptHealth performs its annual impairment assessment of goodwill during the fourth quarter of each year. The impairment assessment can be performed on either a qualitative or quantitative basis. AdaptHealth first assesses qualitative factors to determine whether it is necessary to perform a quantitative goodwill impairment analysis. Under the qualitative assessment, the Company is not required to calculate the fair value of a reporting unit unless the Company determines that it is more likely than not that its fair value is less than its carrying amount. If determined necessary, AdaptHealth applies the quantitative impairment test to identify and measure the amount of impairment, if any, by comparing the fair value of a reporting unit to its carrying amount, including goodwill. If under the quantitative test the fair value of a reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, then the amount of the impairment loss, if any, is determined based on the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds the fair value up to the total value of goodwill assigned to the reporting unit. Fair value determinations require considerable judgment and are sensitive to changes in underlying assumptions and factors, such as estimates of a reporting unit's fair value, and judgment about impairment triggering events. Fair values of the reporting units are estimated using a weighted methodology considering the output from both the income and market approaches. The income approach incorporates the use of a discounted cash flow ("DCF") analysis. A number of significant assumptions and estimates are involved in the application of the DCF model to forecast operating cash flows, including revenue growth rates and discount rates. Several of these assumptions could vary among reporting units. The market approach is performed using the Guideline Public Companies method which is based on earnings multiple data. The Company performs a reconciliation between its market capitalization and its estimate of the aggregate fair value of the reporting units, including consideration of an estimated control premium. As a result, there can be no assurance that the estimates and assumptions made for purposes of the annual or interim goodwill impairment test will prove to be accurate predictions of the future.

AdaptHealth Corp. and subsidiaries ("AdaptHealth" or "the Company") 為提供以患者為中心的居家醫療解決方案的國家領導者，包括居家醫療器材 ("HME"), 醫療用品及相關服務。本公司運作於四個應報告分部，與其產品類別對應：(i) 睡眠健康、(ii) 呼吸道健康、(iii) 糖尿病健康、(iv) 居家 wellness。以下為本公司四個應報告分部所提供之產品與服務說明。
睡眠健康分部提供睡眠治療器材、用品及相關服務 (包括持續正壓通氣及 BiLevel 服務) 給個人用以治療阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症。
呼吸道健康分部提供氧氣及居家機械通氣器材、用品及相關慢性治療服務給個人用以治療呼吸道疾病，例如慢性阻塞性肺病及慢性呼吸道衰竭。
糖尿病健康分部提供醫療器材，包括連續血糖監測器及胰島素泵，以及相關服務給患者用以治療糖尿病。
居家 wellness 分部提供居家醫療器材及服務給患者在其家中，包括那些已從急性醫療機構或其他設施出院的患者。該分部為調整至新生活型態或處理複雜疾病狀態的患者量身打造服務模式，提供必要的醫療用品及耐用醫療器材。
本公司服務受益於 Medicare、Medicaid 及商業保險給付者的對象。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，AdaptHealth 約每年服務 4.3 百萬名患者，遍及美國 50 州，透過我們在 48 州約 640 個據點的網路。本公司的主要營業處所位於賓夕法尼亞州康紹克肯（Conshohocken）東北_lane 路 555 號，5075 號室，郵遞區號 19428。
產品提供。AdaptHealth 提供以患者為中心的居家醫療解決方案，包括居家醫療器材、醫療用品及相關服務，直接送達患者家中，於其從醫院出院及/或收到醫師/醫療轉介後。AdaptHealth 產品的廣度對於急性醫療機構、睡眠實驗室及長期照護機構尤其重要，這些機構會轉介具有複雜病況及多重產品需求的患者。
對於補給銷售及一次性銷售產品，包括那些被視為消耗性產品的項目，AdaptHealth 在產品銷售時收取單筆付款。這些產品包括正壓通氣 ("PAP") 面罩及相關用品、連續血糖監測器 ("CGM")、糖尿病管理用品、骨科支具、傷口照護用品、居家醫療器材及相關配件、失禁用品、藥物、腸內營養用品及其他產品，約佔 AdaptHealth 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年淨銷售額的 63%。
AdaptHealth 會根據美國醫療保險與醫療援助署（"CMS"）或商業保險給付者指定的某些 HME 產品，獲得固定每月金額，例如氧氣與居家機械通氣設備、PAP 設備、醫院病牀及其他產品。這些銷售佔 AdaptHealth 2025 年 12 月 31 日為結算日年度淨營業收入約 33%。
AdaptHealth 在某些風險共擔資本制安排下，會根據每名會員每月（"PMPM"）收取費用，這指的是公司從第三方給付者收取 PMPM 費用，並負責

管理其會員的醫療服務及相關成本。在風險共擔資本制安排下，AdaptHealth 需根據各協議條款，承擔會員所需 contracted 醫療服務的成本。與給付者簽訂的資本制收入合約通常是多年期安排，並具有單一每月 stand ready 表現義務，以根據協議範圍內的條款，為會員在合約期間提供所有必要的醫療照護。這些風險共擔資本制安排佔 AdaptHealth 2025 年 12 月 31 日為結算日年度淨營業收入約 4.0%。

供應鏈。AdaptHealth 在將 HME 產品送達患者家中扮演重要角色。居家醫療設備與糖尿病醫療器材製造商會直接將其產品銷售並運送至 AdaptHealth。AdaptHealth 也會與全國性醫療器材配送公司簽約，將某些 HME 產品與糖尿病醫療器材直接運送至患者家中。這些配送商會在銷售時向 AdaptHealth 計費所運送產品的成本。AdaptHealth 會從多種來源獲得轉介，例如急性醫療機構、睡眠實驗室、肺科與內分泌科診所、長期照護機構、緩和醫療機構運營者與一般門診醫療機構等。AdaptHealth 的產品會由 AdaptHealth 自營或合作的運送貨車送達患者家中，或透過專屬或第三方配送服務運送。AdaptHealth 會直接向給付者與患者計費所送達的產品與所提供的服務。

管理。AdaptHealth 由具備醫療產業多種組織經驗的成熟管理團隊領導。AdaptHealth 的管理架構透過其四個應報告分部進行戰略對齊，每個分部均有總經理負責該分部的運作。這些總經理向 AdaptHealth 的首席運營官報告。AdaptHealth 對關鍵業務流程採用集中化作法，包括收入週期管理、採購、給付者合約、併購（"M&A"）活動、財務、合規、法律、人力資源、資訊科技、補貨與銷售管理。然而，AdaptHealth 認為居家醫療產業特有的患者照護與轉介關係的個別性，也要求在地方層面進行關注。AdaptHealth 透過地方經理迅速且有效地回應地方市場需求與機會，這些經理負責並承擔維護與發展與轉介來源的關係及服務患者的責任。

資訊科技。AdaptHealth 已建立一個整合、科技驅動的集中平台，使其與許多傳統上使用較少自動化流程、通常較複雜、容易出錯且效率較低的競爭對手有所區別。AdaptHealth 的科技使自動化、合規且整合的流程融入患者的照護中。AdaptHealth 認為此先進的科技平台使其在服務患者與醫師的獨特零組件上擁有競爭優勢。AdaptHealth 認為其科技平台有幾個吸引醫師的特點，包括易於使用、透過整合系統提升合規性，以及為患者照護提供的自動化整合流程。AdaptHealth 與第三方軟體供應商建立了緊密的合作關係，以優化其作業流程。此外，AdaptHealth 的電子處方功能提升了透明度，並減少轉錄及其他錯誤。AdaptHealth 認為患者也因從訂單到配送的效率提升及透過 AdaptHealth 平台在各照護點的順暢整合而受益更多。此整合系統也讓 AdaptHealth 管理層能及時獲得關鍵資訊，使其能追蹤公司整體的表現水平。AdaptHealth 使用一項專屬的行動配送科技，稱為 OTL，其具備許多功能，包括配送通知、患者滿意度應用程式及轉介來源通知。

paragraphs: 以下討論應與 AdaptHealth Corp.（"AdaptHealth" 或 "本公司"）合併財務報表及附屬附註一同閱讀，包含於本報告中。所有呈現的金額均依美國通用會計準則（"U.S. GAAP"）記載，除非另有說明。除歷史資訊外，本討論包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險、不確定性與假設，這些因素可能導致實際結果與管理階層預期有重大差異。導致這種差異的因素包括，但不僅限於，本年度10-K表報表第1A項 "風險因素" 所討論的內容。本節中出現的某些金額可能因四捨五入而無法完全相加。
AdaptHealth 是提供以患者為中心的居家醫療解決方案的國家領導者，包括居家醫療設備（"HME"）、醫療用品及相關服務。本公司運作於四個應報告分部，與其產品類別對應：(i) 睡眠健康、(ii) 呼吸道健康、(iii) 糖尿病健康，以及 (iv) 居家 wellness。本公司四個應報告分部所提供的產品與服務描述如下。
睡眠健康分部提供睡眠治療設備、用品及相關服務（包括連續正壓通氣及 BiLevel 服務）給個人，用以治療阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症。
呼吸道健康分部提供氧氣及居家機械通氣設備、用品及相關慢性治療服務給個人，用以治療呼吸道疾病，例如慢性阻塞性肺病及慢性呼吸道衰竭。
糖尿病照護應報告分部提供醫療器材，包括連續血糖監測儀與胰島素泵，以及相關服務，用以協助患者治療糖尿病。
居家健康照護應報告分部為患者在其家中提供居家醫療器材與服務，包括那些已從急性照護機構或其他設施出院的患者。該分部針對正在適應新生活型態或處理複雜疾病狀態的患者，提供必要的醫療用品與耐用醫療器材。
本公司服務受益於 Medicare、Medicaid 及商業保險給付者的對象。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，AdaptHealth 經過其在 48 省約 640 個據點的網路，每年服務約 4.3 百萬名患者，遍及所有 50 省。本公司的主要營業處所位於賓夕法尼亞州康紹克肯（Conshohocken），地址為東北_lane 路 555 號，5075 號室，郵遞區號 19428。

AdaptHealth 購買自供應商並提供給患者的器材與產品的製造與分銷成本，受材料成本、人工費用、運輸及運輸成本（包括燃料成本）影響。目前及未來的通貨膨脹影響可能由多種因素驅動，包括總體經濟的通貨膨脹成本增加、供應鏈中斷以及政府刺激或財政政策。通貨膨脹的增加可能影響 AdaptHealth 產品與服務的整體需求、材料的可得性、其人工、器材與產品的成本、運輸、倉儲及其他營運費用，以及其產品的獲利能力，所有這些都可能對 AdaptHealth 的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流產生不利影響。此外，AdaptHealth 不確定是否能夠將增加的成本轉嫁給客戶以抵銷通貨膨脹壓力。AdaptHealth 因材料、人工、運輸及運輸成本增加而經歷通貨膨脹壓力與較高的成本。儘管已出現通貨膨脹的增加，AdaptHealth 無法預測這些趨勢是否會持續。AdaptHealth 為應對這些通貨膨脹壓力所採取的緩衝措施包括利用 AdaptHealth 的採購實力與供應商進行談判，以及增加使用科技以提高營運效率並控制成本，例如 AdaptHealth 的數位平台用以處理處方箋、訂單與配送。

營業收入。營業收入係針對 AdaptHealth 提供給病患的居家醫療解決方案，包括居家醫療照護（HME）、醫療器材及相關服務所產生的服務及相關產品收入。收入係於銷售供應品及消耗品時確認，或於服務期間內確認（包括，但不限於 PAP 機器、醫院病牀、輪椅及其他設備的設備租賃），扣除預估將從病患處收取的隱含價格讓利金額，或根據與 Medicare、Medicaid 及其他第三方付款人（包括私人保險公司）的補償安排，於病患符合資格接收醫療服務的月份確認。某些趨勢或不確定性可能對收入成長及營運結果產生重大影響，包括本公司能否取得新的風險共擔資本安排、新病患啟動及從病患轉介來源產生轉介，以及考量通貨膨脹壓力下能否滿足增加的需求。
淨營業收入成本。淨營業收入成本主要包含非資本化醫療器材及供應品的成本、分銷費用、勞動成本、場地及車輛租金成本，以及資本化病患設備的折舊費用。分銷費用係指協調並交付產品及服務至病患所產生的成本。分銷費用包含車隊的租賃、維護、授權及燃料成本；駕駛員及調度人員的薪資、福利及其他相關成本；以及支付給貨運公司的金額。
一般及行政費用。一般及行政費用包含公司支持成本，包括收入週期管理成本、資訊科技、人力資源、財務、契約、法律、合規、基於股票的報酬及其它行政成本。
折舊及攤銷費用，排除病患設備折舊。折舊費用包含除病患設備外的資本資產折舊費用（病患設備已包含於淨營業收入成本中）。攤銷費用包含可辨認無形資產的攤銷費用。
AdaptHealth 的營運結果及財務表現受本文件所述期間內某些獨特事件的影響，包括以下內容：

AdaptHealth 在其資產負債表上有相當多的商譽，係因 AdaptHealth 進行的企業併購所致。商譽不進行攤銷，而是每年於報告單位層級評估是否發生減損，並在發生觸發事件或情況變更時評估是否可能減損。判斷是否發生減損指標需要相當多的判斷。可能導致每年或中期進行商譽減損評估的觸發事件包括，但不限於歷史或預測報告單位收入、營運結果或現金流下降，以及 AdaptHealth 股價或市場總值持續下降。這些情況變更可能包括，但不限於法律環境、補償環境、營運表現及未來前景的變更。AdaptHealth 每年第四季進行商譽減損評估。減損評估可以採用質性或量化方式進行。AdaptHealth 首先評估質性因素，以判斷是否需要進行量化商譽減損分析。在質性評估中，除非公司判斷其公平價值可能低於帳面價值，否則公司無需計算報告單位的公平價值。若經判斷為必要，AdaptHealth 會應用量化減損測試，以識別並衡量減損金額（如有），透過比較報告單位的公平價值與其帳面價值（包括商譽）。若在量化測試中報告單位的公平價值低於帳面價值，則減損損失金額（如有）係根據帳面價值超過公平價值的金額，但不超過分配至該報告單位的商譽總價值來計算。公平價值的判斷需要大量判斷，並對基礎假設及因素的變動相當敏感，例如報告單位公平價值的估計，以及減損觸發事件的判斷。報告單位的公平價值係透過加權方法進行估計，考量收入法與市場法的輸出結果。收入法 incorporates 折現現金流（"DCF"）分析。在應用 DCF 模型預測營運現金流時，涉及許多重要的假設與估計，包括收入成長率與折現率。這些假設在不同報告單位間可能有所差異。市場法係透過指引上市公司法進行，基於獲利倍數資料。公司會進行其市場總值與報告單位總體公平價值估計之間的調和，並考量控制 premium 的估計。因此，無法保證用於年度或中期商譽減損測試的估計與假設會準確預測未來。

headings: 與本公司及產業相關之風險
本公司對患者服務設備及用品之供應商依賴程度較高，可能影響其營運能力。
美國供應鏈中斷及總體經濟勞動力短缺已對本公司業務造成負面影響，並可能持續造成負面影響。
本公司已受到，且可能持續受到通貨膨脹及利率上升之影響。
若在風險共擔協議下之費用高於收入，可能對本公司營運成果造成負面影響。
本公司之付款方契約可能被重新協議或終止，導致本公司之營收或利潤減少。
付款方對本公司所提供產品之覆蓋方式所作之變更，可能對本公司之營收及營運造成負面影響。
政府或私人付款方之供應補給排程變更，可能對本公司造成負面影響。
若 AdaptHealth 未能妥善管理複雜且耗時的賠償程序，其營業收入、財務狀況及營運成果可能會受到影響。
AdaptHealth 可能因健康保險公司及其他產業參與者的併購而受到負面影響。
若 AdaptHealth 無法維持或發展與病患轉介來源的關係，其成長與獲利能力可能會受到不利影響。
醫療設備技術的變更及新治療方式的發展，可能導致 AdaptHealth 現有設備或服務變得過時。
AdaptHealth 過去以收購其他公司作為戰略成長計畫，若此計畫無法成功，將會對其產生影響。
AdaptHealth 的營業收入可能因聯邦及州政府對賠償及其他醫療補助與醫療保險政策的變更而受到影響。
paragraphs: 本公司營運環境快速變動，涉及許多風險。以下討論重點說明部分風險，其他風險則於本報告其他部分討論。這些及其它風險可能對本公司業務、營業收入、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。此外，尚有其他未被本公司知悉或目前認為不重要之風險因素，也可能影響本公司業務或營運成果。

AdaptHealth 目前依賴較少的供應商提供其大部分病患服務設備與用品。若發生重大價格上漲，或無法從現有供應商取得這些設備與用品，AdaptHealth 可能被迫使用替代供應商。此外，貿易政策發展，包括持續進行的調查，可能導致進口醫療設備或零組件的新關稅，這可能提高製造或採購病患服務設備與用品的成本。這些關稅或任何對特定醫療設備製造商課徵的新消費稅，可能轉嫁至客戶，例如 AdaptHealth。這些製造商可能被迫對其產品或製造流程進行其他變更，而這些變更對 AdaptHealth 而言可能不可接受，導致必須更換供應商。任何 AdaptHealth 使用的供應商變更，可能導致這些產品的交付延遲及可能的收入損失，這可能對 AdaptHealth 的營運成果造成不利影響。此外，替代供應商可能無法取得，或無法以相似或有利的價格提供其產品與服務。若 AdaptHealth 無法以相似或有利的價格取得目前使用的病患服務設備與用品，或替代品，AdaptHealth 提供這些產品的能力可能受到嚴重影響，這可能對其業務、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流、資本資源及流動性造成不利影響。
許多公司，包括 AdaptHealth，在供應鏈與勞動力方面都面臨挑戰。材料、設備與勞動力短缺、運輸、物流及其他延遲及其它供應鏈相關中斷，可能使 AdaptHealth 更難以取得第三方的產品或服務，且成本更高。若發生這些類型的中斷，可能對 AdaptHealth 的業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流造成重大不利影響。持續的勞動力短缺已導致產業內競爭激烈，以吸引及留住人才，同時也導致勞動成本增加。
罷工活動是另一個可能導致勞動成本增加的因素。AdaptHealth 目前僅有極少數的員工屬於工會，因此工會活動增加可能對 AdaptHealth 的勞動成本造成重大影響。AdaptHealth 若無法招募及留住合格員工，或無法控制勞動成本，可能對其業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流造成重大不利影響。

雖然 AdaptHealth 嘗試緩解任何成本增加、勞動力影響及供應鏈延遲與短缺，但這些努力可能無法成功，AdaptHealth 可能因這些因素而面臨不利影響。AdaptHealth 無法預測這些當前趨勢或未來運營成本增加的程度。若這些成本持續增加，AdaptHealth 可能無法完全或部分將這些成本轉嫁至現有及潛在客戶，或其客戶可能因供應鏈延遲而尋求其他競爭來源，這可能對 AdaptHealth 的業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流造成重大不利影響。

通貨膨脹的增加已對 AdaptHealth 產生，且可能持續產生不利影響。目前及未來的通貨膨脹影響可能由多種因素驅動，包括普遍的通貨膨脹成本增加、供應鏈中斷及政府刺激或財政政策。AdaptHealth 從供應商購入並提供給病患的設備與產品的製造與分銷成本，可能受通貨膨脹壓力及材料、勞動力、運輸及運輸成本（包括燃料成本）的影響。設備與產品的成本也可能因某些產品供應不足而受到影響。此外，AdaptHealth 並不能確定是否能將增加的成本轉嫁至客戶以抵消通貨膨脹壓力。通貨膨脹的增加可能影響 AdaptHealth 產品與服務的總體需求、其勞動力、設備與產品的成本，以及其產品所能實現的毛利率，所有這些都可能對 AdaptHealth 的業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流造成不利影響。此外，未來通貨膨脹的波動性及通貨膨脹對成本及材料可用性、運輸與倉儲成本、勞動力工資壓力及其他營運費用的影響，可能對 AdaptHealth 的財務結果造成不利影響。儘管近期通貨膨脹有所增加，AdaptHealth 無法預測這些趨勢是否會持續。AdaptHealth 面對這些通貨膨脹壓力的主要緩衝措施包括利用 AdaptHealth 的採購力與供應商進行談判，以及增加使用科技以提高營運效率及控制成本，例如 AdaptHealth 的處方箋、訂單及配送數位平台。
